newsitem.title: GERMANY: German DAX closes down, overshadowed by Telekom.
newsitem.headline: German DAX closes down, overshadowed by Telekom.

text.p: Germany's DAX index of leading shares finished lower on Monday as attention was overwhelmingly fixed on market debutant Deutsche Telekom AG, which was able in contrast to post a strong gain in bourse trade.
The DAX-30 share index, which the telecom giant will join on Tuesday -- closed 31.96 points lower at 2,763.84 amid volumes described by traders as weak.
Deutsche Telekom itself opened bourse trade at 33.20 marks, well above its issue price of 28.50, before going on to add a further 70 pfennigs to 33.90 marks at the bourse close.
Trading volume in the share was huge, with some 37.7 million shares changing hands.
"There's only one subject today and that's Telekom. Don't go looking for much action elsewhere in the market," said one Frankfurt trader.

Dealers said the main impact on the stock had been buying by institutions seeking to top up small allocations in the issue, which was heavily-oversubscribed and saw an unparalleled amount of interest by small investors.

"There is still a good chance that it can improve on this (current) level. There are a couple of institutions out there that didn't get much of an allocation but still haven't gone into the market yet," said one trader.
Telekom shares however later eased down to 33.20 over the IBIS all-day electronic trading system. The stock is due to be traded in New York later on Monday and Tokyo on Tuesday.

Opinion was split on the course of the shares over the next few days, with some dealers believing the stock could rise to around 35-36 marks while others thought it had seen its best value for the next few days.
Any small impact arising from smaller investors "stagging" -- taking quick profit -- from their initial investment in the shares could already be fizzling out, one dealer said.
"With the 50 pfennig special discount they got, they will already be quite pleased with the five mark per share profit they have already pocketed, thank you," he added.
Activity elsewhere in the market was limited, with blue chips including engineering and electronics group Siemens AG and pharmaceuticals firm BASF AG both slipping in line with the market.
Traders said the market had been expected to consolidate after its recent run that took it close to the 2,800 point threshold for the first time last week.
December DAX futures fell 20.5 points to 2,789.0.
Retailer Karstadt AG fell 33 marks to 542, reacting to an announcement on Friday that it expected 1996 earnings to be below those in 1995.
